correctness.rationale: For \(n\ge7\), verified L_(C_n^2)=(3I+A)L_C and exact cyclic inverse with \(q=(\sqrt5-3)/2\). This gives both edge-current columns and effective-resistance diagonals. Periodized positive-mass bounds prove long-edge dominance for Q above n=16 and P above n=35. The included exact-rational executable exhaustively verifies every remaining n from \(7\le n\le35\), solving each system and checking all residuals; it also reconstructs direct graph-Laplacian columns for \(7\le n\le12\). Two geometrically decaying positive tails per profile give the stated \(\log n/n\) coefficient and \(O(n^{-1})\) error. Unproved generalizations are explicitly excluded.

originality.rationale: Compared by mathematical implication to the 2014 and 2021 exact-resistance results on the identical squared cycles, as well as 2023 invariant-projection work. All-pairs effective resistance provides the raw matrix entries; the globally maximizing displacement-two edge and shared logarithmic norm correction require a nontrivial absolute-current sign analysis absent from examined statements. Exact claimed novelty is confined to these extra operator-norm assertions. Residual risk of an independently published equivalent or a hidden corollary remains.
residual_risks: Preexisting formulas for all pairwise resistances allow a direct but nontrivial derivation of the new projection-norm statement; specialist work may have carried out this derivation without the terminology used here.

value.rationale: For a natural four-regular Cayley graph family with two competing edge directions, the theorem classifies the exact endpoint cut/cycle projection norms at every size, determines the strictly maximizing edge orbit and derives a shared, nonzero \(\log n/n\) finite-size correction. The oscillatory Green kernel makes the absolute-current signs change at logarithmically many locations, so this is not simply a trace or effective-resistance lookup. Both endpoint invariants are of direct interest in Lipschitz-free and cycle-space Banach geometry.
